findings.highlight: I was told it can give you an advantage.
findings.evidenceJa: 知らなくちゃやっていけないって話だからな。
findings.governingReading: 知らなくちゃやっていけない states necessity in his present situation and does not attribute the conclusion to an unnamed adviser.
findings.explanation: Shirou says he needs Servant identities to manage or survive, but English says he was told they merely provide an advantage.

findings.highlight: I don't intend to seek out someone to fight if they haven't done anything wrong
findings.evidenceJa: 何もしてこないヤツにこっちから戦いに行く気なんてない
findings.governingReading: 何もしてこない describes nonaggression toward Shirou's side, not an objective innocence judgment.
findings.explanation: Shirou refuses to seek combat with someone who has not acted against him; English instead says someone who has done nothing morally wrong.

findings.highlight: He is not famous in this country, so his prominence may be diminished
findings.evidenceJa: この国では知名度が低いですから存在が劣化しています
findings.governingReading: 存在が劣化 describes the Servant's present manifestation or capacity deteriorating in this land.
findings.explanation: Cú Chulainn's manifested existence being degraded by low local renown becomes his prominence being diminished.

findings.highlight: a demonic spear capable of growing a thousand thorns the moment it pierces its enemies.
findings.evidenceJa: 内部から千の棘を生やして相手を絶命させる魔槍
findings.governingReading: 相手を絶命させる explicitly completes that version of the spear tradition with death.
findings.explanation: The thousand internal thorns killing the victim loses the lethal result.

findings.highlight: each of them agrees that the spear always pierces the heart.
findings.evidenceJa: その全てに“心臓を穿つ”という一節が残っている。
findings.governingReading: 一節が残っている identifies a shared transmitted motif before Saber concludes what the weapon actually does.
findings.explanation: A heart-piercing phrase surviving across varied traditions becomes agreement that the spear always pierces the heart.

findings.highlight: It either bends time and space or the law of causality
findings.evidenceJa: 空間をねじ曲げているのか、因果律を変えているのか。
findings.governingReading: 空間をねじ曲げる and changing causality are the two alternatives; time is not named.
findings.explanation: Saber's hypothesis that the spear bends space gains unsupported manipulation of time.

findings.highlight: a single arrow would typically not be effective against Servants.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントには弓矢など当たりません。
findings.governingReading: 当たらない and 命中させられる form an exact failure/success pair, with the heart as the guaranteed target.
findings.explanation: The cannon-and-arrow analogy depends on ordinary arrows failing to hit Servants and Gáe Bolg making the arrow hit the heart; English changes this to general ineffectiveness and potential lethality.

findings.highlight: Lancer appears to be a curious sort of person.
findings.evidenceJa: むらっけのある人物のようです。
findings.governingReading: Saber tentatively describes Lancer as inconsistent or subject to moods, responding to Shirou's contrast between his efficient weapon and wasteful toying.
findings.explanation: Saber's description of Lancer as inconsistent becomes a general remark that he is peculiar. The link between his temperament and his inefficient toying is weakened.

findings.highlight: He may have been quite heartless in history
findings.evidenceJa: 非情な人物ではありましたが
findings.governingReading: 非情な人物ではありましたが is her present character judgment from the encounter, balanced against an unhateful side.
findings.explanation: Saber's direct assessment that Lancer was ruthless becomes uncertainty that he may have been heartless in history.
